facts.text: Oak Park hosts the world’s largest collection of Frank Lloyd Wright buildings, including his former studio now a national historic landmark.
The Oak Park Public Library began as a 1903 public library, celebrated for its rich history and early community role.
In 1905 the CTA Blue Line extended into Oak Park, originally built on tracks laid by the Chicago Aurora & Elgin interurban.
The village’s first railroad depot appeared in 1872 on the Chicago & Northwestern Railway, sparking Oak Park’s rise as a Chicago suburb.
Oak Park’s historic preservation ordinance, first passed in 1972, protects over 2,400 sites, mainly Queen Anne, Prairie School, and Craftsman homes.
Ernest Hemingway’s birthplace and boyhood home, along with Edgar Rice Burroughs’ three residences, are key literary landmarks in Oak Park.
